problem.scene: A care leaver is a green figure on the dashboard.
problem.question: He lives an hour from college, and has stopped going.
without: Departments don't see themselves as parents

problem.standards: Ofsted's 2026 ILACS framework gives care leavers a judgement of their own. The Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 extends the duty to schools, colleges, NHS bodies and government departments.
problem.evidence: Bring a recent board report and your local offer for care leavers. We build the exercises around your own material.

groups: Lead members for children and newly elected councillors

From across the council, not only children's services

outcomes: See a decision from their side
Describe how a board decision, such as where a care leaver lives, feels from the young person's side.
Recognise when a report shows activity rather than children's experiences, and ask the next question.
Explain the seven corporate parenting principles and what the 2026 Act adds, and for whom.
Use Maslow to see what each department offers, and link the board's work to the four ILACS judgements.
Apply "would it be good enough for my child?" to a real decision and a board paper.
Map what each department offers care leavers, name who follows up each gap, and report back to young people.

pillars.title: The 7 corporate parenting principles
pillars.stance: Would it be good enough for my child?
pillars.stance_line: Section 1 of the Children and Social Work Act 2017 asks the council to act as a good parent would.
items: Act in their best interests and promote their health and wellbeing.
Encourage children to say what they think, want and feel.
Take those views, wishes and feelings into account.
Help them get to and make the best use of services.
Promote high aspirations and seek the best outcomes.
Keep them safe, with stability at home, in relationships and at school or work.
Prepare them for adulthood and independent living.
pillars.base: The Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act 2026 extends these responsibilities to schools, colleges, NHS bodies and government departments.

story_line: Four stories run through the day: Kelsey, 17, Jodie, 15, Daniel, 19, and Dominic, 18. Each is a composite, drawn from real experiences of care.

facilitator.name: Luke Rodgers BEM
facilitator.line: From care leaver to care leader
paras: Luke went into care at 10. He has spent his career inside children's services as a consultant, trainer and keynote speaker, and is CEO of The Care Leaders.

He has worked with councils nationally on how they act as corporate parents, including Middlesbrough, where young people and staff co-produced the corporate parenting principles, and Durham, where the Durham Cares vision changed how corporate parenting is understood.
He led the national engagement on England's new fostering standards for the Department for Education, and knows the national policy behind the duty.
He was a Knowledge Equity Fellow at Saïd Business School, University of Oxford, and was awarded the British Empire Medal in 2018 for commitment to children and families.
